FACTS OF THE CASE:
2. The case of the plaintiff as set up in the plaint, in a nutshell, is as under: -
2.1 The plaintiff is the absolute owner and landlady of Stall No.1, including back portion of the Stall No.1, two side open, with roof, situated at Sector-12, Mini Market,
R.K.Puram, New Delhi [hereinafter referred to as the 'Suit Property'].
The detailed dimensions of the suit property are mentioned in the site plan in red colour marked as 'A' & 'B', which has been annexed with the plaint.
2.2 It is stated that the plaintiff is daughter of Sh. Surender Kumar Bajaj, who was real brother of Sh. Moti Ram Bajaj.
Sh. Moti Ram Bajaj was the absolute owner of the suit property and he was employed in PEC Ltd. Company, New Delhi.
The suit property was allotted to him by DDA on 28.03.1981.

2.3 It is averred that since Mr. Moti Ram Bajaj was not married during his life time,
therefore, he had adopted the plaintiff, by way of an adoption deed executed between parents of the plaintiff namely Mrs. and Mr. Surender Bajaj and Sh. Moti Ram Bajaj (adopting father) on 24.3.1999 and since then, the plaintiff was living with her adoptive father Sh.
Moti Ram Bajaj.
2.4

It is further averred that said Sh. Moti Ram Bajaj had unfortunately expired, leaving behind only one legal heir i.e. the plaintiff and thereafter, the plaintiff applied before Hon'ble High Court of Delhi to get a Succession Certificate of the movable and immovable properties of her deceased father namely Sh. Moti Ram Bajaj, wherein, Hon'ble High Court of Delhi had passed Succession order for succession certificate in favour of the plaintiff on 08.09.2005.
Therefore, by virtue of said Succession Certificate, the plaintiff became absolute owner of the suit property.
Subsequently, she applied and got installed electricity connection from BSES in her name in the suit property.
2.5 It is claimed that the defendants were misusing and stealing electricity by tapping the electricity wires directly from BSES Ltd. line.
Besides, it is also claimed that the plaintiff has been continuously paying House Tax of the suit property.
2.6 It is averred that the suit property was let out for commercial use to defendant no.1 on monthly rent of 25,000/- excluding electricity, house tax and other charges on 08.10.2013.

It was agreed between the parties that the defendant no.1 shall pay monthly rent of 25,000/- to the plaintiff,
payable in one month advance, on or before 10th day of every month according to English Calendar month.
Accordingly, the defendant no.1 paid rent up to October, 2016.
Thereafter, the rent was increased by the plaintiff from 25,000/- to 30,000/- per month.
Accordingly, the defendant no.1 paid rent to the plaintiff till October,2018.

The defendant no.1 had also issued one cheque bearing no.789234 dated 20.12.2017 drawn on Indian Overseas Bank on account of rent for the month of December, 2017 in favour of the plaintiff, but the said cheque was also dishonoured on 19.12.2017 due to 'Funds Insufficient'.
The plaintiff then filed a criminal complaint U/s 138 NI Act, qua the aforesaid two cheques against the defendant no.1.The
plaintiff claims that the defendant no.1 is also in arrears of rent for back portion of the suit property from the month of December, 2017.

2.8 The plaintiff further avers that as per terms and conditions of the rent agreement, the defendant no.1 had also agreed that he would pay the electricity charges & water charges of the suit property in addition to the monthly rent, as per meter/sub meter reading and would also pay the maintenance charges directly to RWA/building/society maintenance charges, but, the plaintiff claims that the defendant no.1 neither paid the electricity consumption charges, nor paid any/maintenance charges to RWA/ building/ society, deliberately and intentionally.

2.9 It is alleged that the plaintiff came to know on 10.12.2018 that the defendant no.1 had clandestinely and mala fidely, and in breach of Clause 08 of the Lease Deed dated 08.10.2013,
sub-let back portion/shop of the suit property to defendant nos. 2 &3 without her permission and prior consent in writing.

Consequently, she got issued a legal notice dated 27.11.2018, thereby terminating the tenancy of defendant no.1 and called upon the said defendant and the sub-tenants of defendant no.1 to hand over the vacant and peaceful possession of the suit property to the plaintiff on or before midnight of December 26, 2018, failing which, it was informed that the defendants would be in unauthorized and illegal possession of the suit property, but to no avail.

The plaintiff has further averred that in view of the provisions of Section 106 of the Transfer of Property Act, the tenancy of the defendant no.1 had come to an end after expiry of 30 days from the date of the legal notice expiring with the end of the month of the tenancy.

2.10 It is further averred that the defendants had also encroached upon the Government land to the extent of 6 x 11 ft. in width and this encroachment runs all along the side portion of the suit property.

The portion shown as 6 ft. x 11 ft. is that portion of the land, which belongs to the Government and is shown and marked as green colour in the site plan, on which, the defendants have got no right, title or interest of any nature whatsoever.
The plaintiff further claims that she had sent written complaints to the Deputy Commissioner of MCD, Green Park, New Delhi, BSES Rajdhani Power Ltd. and also to Delhi Jal Board on 26.03.2019.

inter alia, that:-
5.1 The plaintiff has no concern with the tenanted shop, which is totally situated independently on the back portion of the shop that belongs to the plaintiff and had given the same on rent to defendant no.1.

Thus, it is stated that the plaint does not disclose any cause of action against them, which can be adjudicated only after measuring the area of the tenanted shop which belongs to the plaintiff, on the basis of relevant documents of the tenanted shop and the shop in possession of defendant no.2 does not fall within the said area of the tenanted shop, which belongs to the plaintiff.

5.2 The present suit has been filed by plaintiff in collusion with defendant no.1 in order to extort money from defendant no.2 and also to forfeit the security amount of 6,00,000/-, which was given by defendant No.2 to defendant no.1 when the property in question was rented out to defendant no.2 @ 12,000/- per month.

5.3 The plaintiff in collusion with defendant no.1, has filed the present suit despite the fact that the property in question which is in possession of defendant no.2, does not belong to the plaintiff and the defendant no.1, in collusion with the plaintiff, has cheated defendant no.2 and has taken the amount as stated above for security of the property in question in possession of defendant no.2 after impersonating himself as the owner and the plaintiff has no concern with the property in possession of defendant no.2 as the tenanted shop is completely different from the shop in possession of defendant no. 2 and there is no relationship between the plaintiff and the said defendants as landlord and tenant as the shop in their possession does not fall in the area of the tenanted shop.

sentences.text: As already noted above, the plaintiff has examined herself as PW1 and deposed on the lines of the averments made in the plaint during her examination-in-chief by way of affidavit in evidence Ex.PW1/A (sic).

She also deposed to have lodged written complaint dated 26-3-2019 with Deputy Commissioner MCD, Green Park, New Delhi, BSES Rajdhani Power Ltd. and also to Delhi Jal Board and exhibited the said complaints along with recent photographs of the suit property as Ex.PW1/G (Colly.).

Nevertheless, it is found from records that the plaintiff has failed to disclose any basis either in the plaint or even during the trial, on the basis of which the allegations regarding encroachment on government land are founded.

In case the defendants have encroached upon any particular portion of the government land, then it was incumbent upon the plaintiff to disclose particulars of such land owning Authority and also to implead such agency as co-defendant in the present suit.

Moreover, this Court is of the view that it is not within the domain of plaintiff to seek such relief in the form of mandatory injunction against either of the defendants for removing alleged encroachment on the government land under the garb of the present suit.
It is basically the right of the land owning agency to initiate appropriate legal proceedings against these defendants for removal of encroachment on government land in accordance with law.
As per the own case of the plaintiff, the portion admeasuring 6x11 ft. shown in Green Colour in the Site Plan does not belong to her.

That being so, this Court is of the view that the plaintiff has no locus- standi to seek any direction to either of the defendants to remove alleged encroachment from the government land by way of the present suit.
This is more so, when there is no cogent and reliable evidence to show that either of these defendants has actually encroached upon any portion of the government land.
Moreover, the plaintiff has also failed to disclose the relevant details regarding date, month or year when such alleged encroachment took place.
She has also not disclosed as to which of the defendants had encroached upon said portion and how she has got any locus standi to seek the relief of mandatory injunction.

For all these reasons, this Court is of the view that the plaintiff has miserably failed to prove this issue even on the basis of preponderance of probability and thus, she is not entitled to any relief of mandatory injunction in terms of prayer clause no. 22(d) of the plaint.

However, it is hereby expressly made clear that nothing mentioned or observed herein above shall be construed as any findings in favour of either of the defendants insofar as the portion shown in green colour in the site plan is concerned.

This Court, while deciding this issue, has not concluded that either of the defendants has got any right, title or interest whatsoever in respect of the said portion and said question is left open to be decided in appropriate proceedings, if any, to be initiated by the rightful claimant, in accordance with the law.
This issue stands decided in these terms.

sentences.text: The entire claim of plaintiff regarding her ownership in respect of shop shown at Point B in the Site Plan, is basically founded upon the Succession Order dated 08-09-2005 [Ex.PW1/C] passed by Hon'ble High Court of Delhi.

However, there is no mention of any particular area or dimension of Stall No.1 in the Schedule of Assets mentioned in the said order, without which, this Court is not in a position to appreciate or sustain her claim of ownership over the said shop at point B.

This conclusion stands further fortified from the fact that the plaintiff alleged to have let out back portion shown at point 'B' in the Site Plan to defendant no.1 on 15-12-2013 without execution of any rent agreement.

Past conduct of the parties i.e. the plaintiff and the defendant no.1, would demonstrate that the lease agreement dated 08-10-2013 had been executed between them in the past in respect of Stall No.1 shown at Point 'A' in the Site Plan.

Thus, there was no reason as to why similar Lease Agreement would not have been executed at the time of letting out of the back portion shown at Point 'B' in the Site Plan by plaintiff to defendant no.1, as alleged.

This is more so, when such alleged tenancy is claimed to have been created for a period of 72 months, as testified by PW1 during her cross-examination dated 04-10-2024.
43.

Further, the plaintiff has averred in the plaint and has also deposed during her examination-in-chief that the defendant no.1 had paid rent at the rate of 7,700/ - per month in respect of shop shown at point 'B' from 15-12-2013 up to November, 2017, where-after, the rent was increased from 7,700/- to 8,400/- and the defendant no.1 had also paid the rent at such increased rate till November, 2017.However
, the entire plaint, as also testimony of PW1/ plaintiff is silent about mode through which the said rent for the portion shown at point B, was received by her.

Be that as it may, in case the plaintiff would have received any rent at the rate of 7,700/ - per month and subsequently at the rate of 8,400/ - in respect of back portion shown as Shop at point 'B', then she would have definitely disclosed her rental income in her Income Tax Returns (ITRs) filed by her during the relevant period.

Although, the plaintiff as PW1 deposed during her cross-examination on behalf of defendant no.1 that she had shown monthly income received from defendant no.1 in ITR but did not file the same on record.

Not only this, she has also not filed any bank statement reflecting therein relevant entries, if any, regarding monthly rent received by her from defendant no.1 in respect of back portion shown as Shop at Point B in the Site Plan.

44. Although, the defendant no.1 has not filed any written statement in this matter, as a result whereof, his defence was struck off, and thus, this Court could not have the benefit of going through his defence with respect to the claim of the plaintiff regarding letting out of back portion at Point 'B'
to him on 15-12-2013

that there was no arrangement between the plaintiff and the defendant no.1 with respect to payment of rent in respect of shop shown as Point 'B'.
45.

As regards the plea raised in the plaint that the cheques issued by defendant no.1 were dishonoured and she had already filed complaint cases under S. 138 N.I. Act against the said defendant, it may be noted that PW1 has admitted during her cross-examination on behalf of Neha Bajaj vs Charan Preet Singh And Ors on 27 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/100375730/

46. There cannot be any dispute to the legal position laid down by Hon'ble Delhi High Court in the cited case of Anita Jain (supra ) relied on behalf of plaintiff.
However, the said judgment is entirely distinguishable from the facts and circumstances of the present case.

In the cited decision, the petitioner had filed an eviction petition under S. 14(1) (e) read with S. 25B of DRC Act on the ground of bona fide requirement, wherein leave to defend application moved by tenant was dismissed and an eviction order was passed against the respondent / tenant, against which the respondent / tenant preferred revision petition before Hon'ble Delhi High Court.

The tenant had raised a plea in her leave to defend application that she had taken the tenanted premises on rent from erstwhile owner,
as also that there was an understanding between the tenant and said previous owner that she would not be evicted from the tenanted premises.
Further, the tenant had also challenged the ownership of the petitioner/subsequent owner namely Sh. Praveen Kumar Jain.

In this backdrop, Hon'ble Delhi High Court while referring to S. 116 of Indian Evidence Act, as also to the relevant judgments of Hon'ble Apex Court on the point in issue, held that the tenant was estopped from challenging the ownership of the petitioner by virtue of principle of estoppel embodied in S. 116 of the said Act.

In the case in hand, the plaintiff, as already noted above, has failed to prove during trial that the shop shown at Point 'B' in the Site Plan [Ex.PW1/A] was allotted to Sh. Moti Ram Bajaj / her predecessor in interest, and also that she had let out the said portion to defendant no.1 at any point of time.

47. In view of the foregoing reasons and the discussions made hereinabove, this Court is of the considered opinion that the plaintiff has not only failed to prove that she is the rightful owner/claimant of back portion termed as Shop shown at point 'B' in the Site Plan (Ex. PW1/A), but also that she had actually let out the said portion to defendant no.1 either on 15-12-2013 or at any other point of time.
Thus, the plaintiff is held not entitled to decree of possession qua said portion shown at point 'B' in the Site Plan (Ex.PW1/A).

As a necessary corollary thereof, the plaintiff is also held not entitled to the relief regarding decree of prohibitory injunction for restraining the defendants from letting out, transferring, selling, alienating and/or sub-letting the portion shown at point 'B' in the site plan or from creating third party interest in the said portion.

48. Before parting with discussion, it is hereby expressly made clear that while declining the relief of possession in respect of portion termed as Shop B in the Site Plan in favour of plaintiff, this Court has not given any finding that either of the defendants herein, is either owner or even in lawful occupation/possession of the said portion at point B in any manner whatsoever.

Thus, the findings rendered by this Court while deciding these issues, would not create any right, title or interest of any sort whatsoever and for any intent and purposes whatsoever in favour of either of the defendants.
Further, the rightful claimant/owner shall be well within its right to take recourse to appropriate legal remedy in respect of said portion against either of the defendants in accordance with law.
49. The issue nos. 2, 5 and 9 stands decided in the aforesaid terms.

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
Even otherwise, it is relevant to note that such objection is quite vague inasmuch as the said defendants themselves are not aware as to whether said portion shown as Shop at point B is owned by DDA or MCD.
Nevertheless, it is found from records that the plaintiff has failed to disclose any basis either in the plaint or even during the trial, on the basis of which the allegations regarding encroachment on government land are founded.
In case the defendants have encroached upon any particular portion of the government land, then it was incumbent upon the plaintiff to disclose particulars of such land owning Authority and also to implead such agency as co-defendant in the present suit.
Moreover, this Court is of the view that it is not within the domain of plaintiff to seek such relief in the form of mandatory injunction against either of the defendants for removing alleged encroachment on the government land under the garb of the present suit.
It is basically the right of the land owning agency to initiate appropriate legal proceedings against these defendants for removal of encroachment on government land in accordance with law.
As per the own case of the plaintiff, the portion admeasuring 6x11 ft. shown in Green Colour in the Site Plan does not belong to her.
That being so, this Court is of the view that the plaintiff has no locus- standi to seek any direction to either of the defendants to remove alleged encroachment from the government land by way of the present suit.
This is more so, when there is no cogent and reliable evidence to show that either of these defendants has actually encroached upon any portion of the government land.
Moreover, the plaintiff has also failed to disclose the relevant details regarding date, month or year when such alleged encroachment took place.
She has also not disclosed as to which of the defendants had encroached upon said portion and how she has got any locus standi to seek the relief of mandatory injunction.
For all these reasons, this Court is of the view that the plaintiff has miserably failed to prove this issue even on the basis of preponderance of probability and thus, she is not entitled to any relief of mandatory injunction in terms of prayer clause no. 22(d) of the plaint.
The plaintiff had to prove her right to recover the vacant and peaceful possession of the said backside portion from the said two defendants.
35. For the said purpose, the plaintiff has solely relied upon three documents i.e. the Order/judgment dated 08-09-2005 passed in Test Cas. No.12/2001 titled as ' Neha Bajaj v. The State' (Ex.PiW1/C) passed by Hon'ble Delhi High Court, electricity bills and house tax payment receipts.
36.
Neha Bajaj vs Charan Preet Singh And Ors on 27 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/100375730/
13 38.
There is no gainsaying that the said document is filed by the plaintiff herself along with the plaint.
A bare perusal of the said agreement would reveal that the description of the rented property has been mentioned therein, as Stall No.1, thereby leaving no scope of any doubt that Stall No.1 (supra) constitutes the entire property as a whole, and which had been let out by plaintiff to defendant no.1.
39.
Had there been a situation where back portion shown as Shop at Point B in the Site Plan, would have also formed part of the suit property, as is alleged by plaintiff, then the said Lease/ Rent Agreement would recite that part or portion of the property bearing Stall No.1, Mini Market,
Sector-12, R. K. Puram, New Delhi was being let out by plaintiff to defendant no.1, which is not the situation herein.
It is nowhere the case of the plaintiff throughout the trial that Stall No.1 shown at Point A in the Site Plan and back-side portion shown as Shop at Point B in the Site Plan, were different properties owned by Late Sh. Moti Ram Bajaj and same were subsequently inherited by her.
Rather, it is the specific case of the plaintiff as stated in Para no.1 of the plaint itself that she is the absolute owner/ land lady of Stall No.1 including back portion thereof with roof, situated at Sector-12, Mini Market, R.K.Puram, New Delhi and both the said portions had been let out by her to defendant no.1, albeit on two different occasions and both the portions have been commonly referred to as the suit property therein.
The entire claim of plaintiff regarding her ownership in respect of shop shown at Point B in the Site Plan, is basically founded upon the Succession Order dated 08-09-2005 [Ex.PW1/C] passed by Hon'ble High Court of Delhi.
Past conduct of the parties i.e. the plaintiff and the defendant no.1, would demonstrate that the lease agreement dated 08-10-2013 had been executed between them in the past in respect of Stall No.1 shown at Point 'A' in the Site Plan.
Thus, there was no reason as to why similar Lease Agreement would not have been executed at the time of letting out of the back portion shown at Point 'B' in the Site Plan by plaintiff to defendant no.1, as alleged.
47. In view of the foregoing reasons and the discussions made hereinabove, this Court is of the considered opinion that the plaintiff has not only failed to prove that she is the rightful owner/claimant of back portion termed as Shop shown at point 'B' in the Site Plan (Ex. PW1/A), but also that she had actually let out the said portion to defendant no.1 either on 15-12-2013 or at any other point of time.
Thus, the plaintiff is held not entitled to decree of possession qua said portion shown at point 'B' in the Site Plan (Ex.PW1/A).
Thus, the findings rendered by this Court while deciding these issues, would not create any right, title or interest of any sort whatsoever and for any intent and purposes whatsoever in favour of either of the defendants.
